description: VMware vSphere, Hyper-V, and KVM virtual infrastructure — host contention, VM sprawl, and capacity planning.
name: Virtualization
quickFacts: Install Splunk Add-on for VMware and connect to vCenter to pull ESXi host and VM performance data.

useCases.title: ESXi Host CPU Contention
useCases.value: CPU ready time measures how long a VM waits for physical CPU. High values (>5%) mean the host is overcommitted and VMs are starved for compute.

useCases.title: ESXi Host Memory Ballooning
useCases.value: Memory ballooning means the hypervisor is reclaiming memory from VMs. Swapping at the hypervisor level is worse — causes severe VM performance degradation invisible to the guest OS.

useCases.title: Datastore Capacity Trending
useCases.value: A full datastore prevents VM disk writes, causing crashes and corruption. Datastores fill gradually from VM growth, snapshots, and log accumulation.

useCases.title: Datastore Latency Spikes
useCases.value: Storage latency >20ms significantly impacts VM performance. Detects SAN issues, datastore contention, or storage path problems before applications are affected.

useCases.title: VM Snapshot Sprawl
useCases.value: Old snapshots consume datastore space exponentially, degrade VM I/O performance, and complicate backups. Snapshots >72 hours old are generally a problem.

useCases.title: vMotion Tracking
useCases.value: Tracks VM migrations for troubleshooting and change management. Excessive vMotion can indicate DRS instability or resource contention.

useCases.title: HA Failover Events
useCases.value: HA failover means a host failed and VMs were restarted on surviving hosts. Indicates hardware failure and potential capacity risk on remaining hosts.

useCases.title: DRS Imbalance Detection
useCases.value: DRS should keep clusters balanced. Frequent or failed DRS recommendations indicate resource constraints, affinity rule conflicts, or misconfiguration.

useCases.title: VM Sprawl Detection
useCases.value: Orphaned, powered-off, or idle VMs waste storage, IP addresses, backup capacity, and licenses. Regular cleanup frees significant resources.

useCases.title: vSAN Health Monitoring
useCases.value: vSAN is the storage fabric for many VMware clusters. Degraded vSAN health can cause VM data loss and cluster-wide outages.

useCases.title: ESXi Host Hardware Alerts
useCases.value: CIM-based hardware health detects physical component failures (fans, PSU, temperature) at the hypervisor level before they cause host failure.

useCases.title: VM Resource Over-Allocation
useCases.value: VMs consistently using <20% of allocated CPU/memory waste resources that other VMs could use. Right-sizing saves money and improves cluster capacity.

useCases.title: vCenter Alarm Correlation
